focus: ECharts data, legends, ARIA, decals, and SVG titles
noveltyJustification: Current Apache ECharts Handbook pages verify dataset separation, upper-right legends, scroll controls, toggling, generated aria-label descriptions, and decal support, but the ARIA page inconsistently names aria.enabled after using aria.show. MDN and the W3C editors draft support title/desc accessibility while narrowing the tooltip guarantee to usually/often. The pinned corpus has T1 and rule-10 accessibility, but not T10 pattern fills.
keyQuestions: Which ECharts and SVG accessibility claims are current?
Which requested accessibility capabilities are present in the pinned corpus?
answeredQuestions: ECharts dataset separates data from configuration and supports reuse; the corpus has a deliberate one-file analogue.
ECharts documents upper-right legends, scrollable legend controls, and click-to-toggle categories.
ECharts AriaComponent can generate an aria-label when aria.show is true, and ECharts 5 supports aria.decal.show, subject to a handbook spelling inconsistency.
SVG title is broadly available since July 2015 and usually produces a tooltip while providing an accessible short description; W3C draft guidance covers title/desc and ARIA associations.
T1 and rule-10 accessibility are shipped at the pinned commit; T10 pattern/decal fills remain absent.
ruledOutDirections: Treating runtime-generated ECharts descriptions as the corpus data-table fallback.
Treating tooltip display as universal keyboard/touch coverage.
Treating aria.enabled as a verified ECharts option spelling.
